section_summary: This section details diplomatic correspondence between September 1931 and April 1933 concerning radio interference caused by Japanese stations. Initial documents address complaints from American and Philippine amateur operators regarding Japanese commercial encroachment on amateur bands. Later correspondence focuses on interference with U.S. Army trans-Pacific circuits and U.S. Navy communications in the Far East, culminating in Japanese frequency adjustments and the installation of crystal control equipment at Osaka.

subfiles.about: Transmits correspondence from the Governor General of the Philippine Islands regarding amateur radio interference by Japanese commercial stations.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of War transmits correspondence concerning a complaint from amateur operator I. S. Liner regarding Japanese commercial stations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Forwards letters regarding amateur radio frequency infringements by Japanese stations for transmission to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Ruiz transmits correspondence concerning amateur frequency infringements by Japanese commercial stations, noting international representation belongs to State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Director of Posts Juan Ruiz to Secretary of Commerce and Communications
subfiles.to: Secretary of Commerce and Communications, Manila

subfiles.about: Explains lack of jurisdiction to intervene directly and advises complaining through Philippine authorities.
subfiles.from: International Bureau of the Telegraph Union, Berne
subfiles.summary: The Berne Bureau advises Liner that station control belongs exclusively to national administrations and suggests contacting Philippine authorities.
subfiles.title: Letter from International Bureau of the Telegraph Union to I. S. Liner

subfiles.about: Sollicits assistance from the international bureau against commercial stations trespassing on amateur radio bands.
subfiles.summary: Liner appeals to the Bureau to assist amateurs against commercial station encroachment on allocated frequency bands.
subfiles.title: Letter from I. S. Liner to International Radiotelegraphic Bureau

subfiles.about: Complains of Japanese commercial radio stations operating within the 7000 to 7300 kHz amateur band.
subfiles.summary: Liner protests Japanese commercial stations JBK, JES, and JFH operating inside the 7000–7300 kHz amateur band and requests interference be eliminated.
subfiles.title: Letter from I. S. Liner to Japanese Minister of Communications

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Liner's complaint and states instructions were previously sent to the Tokyo Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Castle acknowledges receipt of the complaint and notes the Tokyo Embassy was previously instructed to request elimination of Japanese commercial interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to Acting Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Reports on diplomatic notes exchanged with the Japanese Foreign Minister concerning radio interference.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Neville transmits copies of Embassy notes and the Japanese Foreign Minister's reply reporting frequency adjustments made at several Japanese stations.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 356 from Edwin L. Neville to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Requests Japanese authorities eliminate interference to American amateur radio stations west of the Rocky Mountains.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Neville informs Shidehara of American Radio Relay League reports of Japanese stations causing broad-note interference in amateur bands, requesting corrective action.
subfiles.title: Embassy Note No. 90 from Edwin L. Neville to Baron Kijuro Shidehara
subfiles.to: Baron Kijuro Shidehara, Minister for Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Forwards complaint from Manila amateur operator regarding interference by Japanese stations JES and JBK.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Neville brings a complaint from Manila regarding Japanese stations JES and JBK encroaching on the 7000–7300 kHz amateur band.
subfiles.title: Embassy Note No. 91 from Edwin L. Neville to Baron Kijuro Shidehara
subfiles.to: Baron Kijuro Shidehara, Minister for Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Reports frequency adjustments at Japanese stations JYZ, JEW, JBK, JFB, and JTY.
subfiles.from: Baron Kijuro Shidehara, Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.summary: Shidehara reports changes made in operating frequencies of five Japanese stations and instructions issued to maintain exact frequencies.
subfiles.title: Foreign Office Note No. 118/T2 from Baron Kijuro Shidehara to Edwin L. Neville
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires a.i.

subfiles.about: Informs the Federal Radio Commission of frequency adjustments made by Japanese radio stations.
subfiles.summary: Castle informs Saltzman that Japanese authorities adjusted frequencies at five stations to resolve amateur interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to Chairman, Federal Radio Commission
subfiles.to: Major General C. McK. Saltzman, Chairman, Federal Radio Commission

subfiles.about: Advises the ARRL of frequency adjustments made at five Japanese stations.
subfiles.summary: Castle notifies Warner that Japanese stations adjusted frequencies, expressing hope that interference with American amateurs will cease.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to K. B. Warner
subfiles.to: K. B. Warner, Secretary, American Radio Relay League

subfiles.about: Acknowledges notification of frequency adjustments made by Japanese stations.
subfiles.from: Major General C. McK. Saltzman, Chairman, FRC
subfiles.summary: Saltzman acknowledges receipt of State Department letter concerning frequency changes at Japanese radio stations.
subfiles.title: Letter from C. McK. Saltzman to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Expresses appreciation for State Department assistance and notes Japanese stations vacated amateur bands.
subfiles.summary: Warner thanks the State Department and reports that Japanese stations appear to have vacated amateur bands.
subfiles.title: Letter from K. B. Warner to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Reports serious interference to U.S. naval radio service in the Far East from Japanese and French stations.
subfiles.summary: Adams reports serious interference to naval radio in the Far East from Japanese and French stations, requesting diplomatic representations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: File cross-reference sheet for decimal file 894.74.
subfiles.summary: File reference sheet noting decimal classification 894.74.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for 894.74

subfiles.about: Directs the Ambassador to informally request Japanese authorities check operating frequencies causing naval interference.
subfiles.summary: Castle instructs Forbes to inform Japanese authorities of interference to American naval radio stations caused by Japanese stations.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 225 from Department of State to W. Cameron Forbes
subfiles.to: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports continued interference experienced by Sixteenth Naval District stations from foreign stations.
subfiles.summary: Adams reports interference to Far East naval radio stations from Japanese, Dutch East Indies, Indo-China, and Siamese stations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: States that diplomatic officers were instructed to request foreign authorities check operating frequencies.
subfiles.summary: Castle informs the Secretary of the Navy that appropriate officers were instructed to request foreign authorities check offending radio frequencies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic representations regarding station JYT in Tokyo interfering with Army station WTJ in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Hurley requests diplomatic representations to Japan regarding station JYT operating on 8160 kHz and interfering with Army station WTJ at Fort Shafter.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Instructs the Ambassador to request Japan eliminate interference by station JYT with Army station WTJ.
subfiles.summary: Castle cites the 1927 International Radio Convention and instructs Forbes to request elimination of interference caused by Tokyo station JYT to Army station WTJ.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 223 from Department of State to W. Cameron Forbes
subfiles.to: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Informs the War Department that the Tokyo Ambassador was requested to seek elimination of station JYT's interference.
subfiles.summary: Castle informs Hurley that the Ambassador at Tokyo has been instructed to seek elimination of interference on 8160 kHz.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Reports on the opening, technical specifications, and commercial implications of broadcasting station JOSK at Kokura.
subfiles.from: Henry B. Hitchcock, American Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.summary: Consul Hitchcock reports on the opening of broadcasting station JOSK at Kokura, describing its technical equipment, coverage in Kyushu, and potential effects on receiver sales.
subfiles.title: Consular Report: New Radio Broadcasting Station at Kokura, Japan

subfiles.about: Explains addressing instructions to regional consulates rather than The Hague or Paris to check frequency deviations.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum explains that consuls can informally suggest station managers check operating frequency deviations without formal diplomatic protests.
subfiles.title: Treaty Division Memorandum regarding regional consular instructions

subfiles.about: Advises on drafting instructions and telegram to Tokyo regarding radio interference in the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: FE comments on timing of instructions to Tokyo and suggests shortening the proposed telegram and altering the letter to War.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum regarding telegram to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports continued high-power non-essential interference from Japanese stations disrupting Honolulu-Manila communications.
subfiles.summary: Hurley urges stronger representations after the Philippine Department reports Japanese stations JYR, JYV, and JYT disrupt 8160 kHz traffic with non-essential signals.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Advises that Tokyo Embassy was asked to telegraph a report on Japanese actions to eliminate interference.
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: White informs Hurley that the Tokyo Embassy was instructed to telegraph a report regarding Japanese actions to eliminate 8160 kHz interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State to Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy to notify Japan of continued disruption of Honolulu-Manila Army communications on 8160 kHz.
subfiles.summary: Stimson instructs the Embassy to inform the Japanese Government that stations JYR, JYV, and JYT disrupt communications, requesting a telegraphic report.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 61 from Secretary of State to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Foreign Office stated Communications Department is communicating directly with interested parties.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Forbes reports that the Japanese Department of Communications is contacting parties directly to settle technical radio matters more rapidly.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 87 from W. Cameron Forbes to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Embassy report that Japanese Communications Department is handling adjustments directly.
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: White conveys the Tokyo Embassy's report that Japanese communications authorities are pursuing direct contact to adjust technical radio interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State to Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Forwards Japanese Foreign Office response and station list denying interference with U.S. Navy frequencies.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Neville transmits the Foreign Office's statement that Japanese stations are operating on registered international frequencies without causing interference to U.S. naval operations.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 551 from Edwin L. Neville to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Lists call signals, locations, and frequencies of Japanese stations communicating across the region.
subfiles.summary: Table listing Japanese stations at Taihoku, Otchishi, Giran, Tokyo, Dairen, and Osaka with their respective call signs and operating frequencies.
subfiles.title: List of Japanese Radio Stations and Operating Frequencies

subfiles.about: Transmits copy of Despatch No. 551 from Tokyo reporting results of protest against Japanese radio interference.
subfiles.summary: Castle transmits to the Secretary of the Navy a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 551 concerning Japanese station frequencies.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Indicates file 894.74/104 was cancelled and transferred to 851G.74/.
subfiles.summary: Department slip recording cancellation of document 894.74/104 and cross-referencing file 851G.74/.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference and Cancellation Sheet for 894.74/104

subfiles.about: Reports interference on 13305 kHz from unlisted Japanese station JEA at Osaka.
subfiles.summary: Adams reports Sixteenth Naval District complaints of serious interference on 13,305 kHz from Japanese station JEA at Osaka, requesting diplomatic representation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Advises that Tokyo Embassy was cabled to request a check on station JEA's assigned frequency.
subfiles.summary: Castle informs the Navy Department that the Tokyo Embassy was cabled to request an investigation into station JEA's operating frequency.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy to request verification of station JEA's operating frequency on 13305 kHz.
subfiles.summary: Castle instructs the Embassy to request Japanese authorities check whether Osaka station JEA is remaining on its assigned frequency.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 102 from Acting Secretary of State to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-references Navy letter of November 1, 1932 filed under 847.74/39 regarding Osaka stations.
subfiles.summary: File note cross-referencing Navy letter regarding Sixteenth Naval District interference from Osaka stations, filed under 847.74/39.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for 894.74/106

subfiles.about: Reports opening of a new coastal wireless station at Aino, replacing the Osezaki station.
subfiles.from: Henry B. Hitchcock, American Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.summary: Consul Hitchcock reports the closure of Japan's first coastal wireless station at Osezaki and the opening of a modern replacement station JOS at Aino.
subfiles.title: Consular Report: New Coastal Wireless Station in Nagasaki Prefecture

subfiles.about: Details Lieutenant Freseman's request for urgent representations to Japan regarding persistent interference on 13308 kHz.
subfiles.summary: Whittington records Lieutenant Freseman's urgent representations concerning persistent interference to naval radio from Osaka stations, summarizing past correspondence and recommending action.
subfiles.title: Treaty Division Memorandum regarding Navy complaint of interference on 13308 kHz

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy to make urgent representations against continued interference on 13308 kHz.
subfiles.summary: Stimson instructs Ambassador Grew to make urgent representations requesting Japanese authorities stop increasing interference to naval communications on 13308 kHz.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 9 from Secretary of State to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports remodeling of Osaka transmitters with crystal control and renewal of urgent representations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Osaka transmitters were remodeled with crystal control to ensure frequency stability, and notes he renewed representations to the Foreign Minister.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 31 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Informs the Navy of Tokyo Embassy's report on crystal control installation at Osaka stations.
subfiles.summary: Castle conveys Ambassador Grew's report stating Osaka transmitting apparatus was remodeled with crystal control to prevent further interference with Philippine naval stations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Reports severe commercial and dotter interference on 8090 kHz from unlisted Japanese station JAQ.
subfiles.summary: Adams reports heavy daily interference on 8090 kHz from station JAQ disrupting Sixteenth Naval District traffic, requesting representations under international radio regulations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits instruction for Tokyo Embassy to protest interference by station JAQ on 8090 kHz.
subfiles.summary: The Department instructs Shanghai to relay by mail to Tokyo a complaint regarding obliterative interference on 8090 kHz caused by station JAQ.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 16 from Secretary of State to American Consul General, Shanghai

subfiles.about: Notes receipt of Tokyo Despatch No. 258 enclosing Japanese note regarding Osaka stations.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum noting that Tokyo Despatch No. 258 enclosing Vice Minister Arita's note was previously received and communicated to Navy.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 258

subfiles.about: Encloses correspondence exchanged with the Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs regarding Osaka stations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards copies of correspondence with Vice Minister Arita concerning Sixteenth Naval District interference from Osaka stations JES and JEA.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 258 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Complains of persistent interference on 13305 kHz caused by Osaka stations JES and JEA.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Counsellor of Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Neville informs Arita that measurements show unstable frequencies from Osaka stations JES and JEA causing serious interference to naval radio stations in the Philippines.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin L. Neville to Hachiro Arita
subfiles.to: Hachiro Arita, Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: States Osaka stations lacked crystal control but were remodeled to ensure frequency stability.
subfiles.from: Hachiro Arita, Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.summary: Arita explains that Osaka transmitters lacked crystal control, but apparatus was remodeled on crystal control system to eliminate future interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hachiro Arita to Edwin L. Neville
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, Counsellor of Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador to bring Osaka station interference on 13305 kHz to Japanese attention.
subfiles.summary: Castle instructs Grew to request Japanese authorities eliminate persistent interference on 13305 kHz caused by Osaka stations JES and JEA.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 129 from Department of State to Joseph C. Grew
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Directs that telegram be transmitted via Naval Radio.
subfiles.summary: Treaty Division routing note directing that the accompanying telegram be dispatched via Naval Radio.
subfiles.title: Treaty Division Routing Slip regarding transmission of telegram

subfiles.about: Requests representations regarding interference to Army channels from station JAQ and Taihoku station JFI.
subfiles.summary: Hurley requests diplomatic representations against interference to trans-Pacific Army circuits caused by station JAQ and Taihoku station JFI, citing international priority.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Instructs Shanghai to mail instruction to Tokyo Embassy to protest interference by JAQ and JFI.
subfiles.summary: Stimson instructs Shanghai to forward an instruction to Tokyo protesting interference to Army operations in San Francisco and Manila from stations JAQ and JFI.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 22 from Secretary of State to American Consul General, Shanghai

subfiles.about: Confirms appropriate representations were made to the Foreign Office regarding station JAQ.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew confirms that appropriate diplomatic representations concerning station JAQ interference were made to the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 42 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Encloses Embassy memorandum and Japanese Foreign Office reply regarding crystal control at Osaka.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits copies of the Embassy memorandum left with the Vice Minister and the Japanese Foreign Office response regarding frequency stabilization at Osaka.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 287 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Urges Japanese authorities to take measures correcting frequency deviation of Osaka stations.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy memorandum urges Japanese authorities to take urgent measures to keep Osaka stations within assigned bands, noting worsening interference on 13308 kHz.
subfiles.title: Embassy Memorandum handed to Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Reports test measurements confirming Osaka station's frequency stabilized on 13280 kHz via crystal control.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office states Osaka began operating crystal control equipment on January 15, with Tokyo test measurements confirming stable frequencies around 13,280 kHz.
subfiles.title: Foreign Office Memorandum No. 5/T2 in reply to American Embassy

subfiles.about: Transmits copy of Despatch No. 287 from Tokyo regarding Osaka radio stations.
subfiles.summary: State Department compliments slip transmitting copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 287 to the Secretary of the Navy.
subfiles.title: State Department Transmittal Note to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Confirms representations were made to the Foreign Office regarding JAQ and JFI interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that appropriate representations were made to the Japanese Foreign Office concerning interference caused by stations JAQ and JFI.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 51 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Foreign Office inquires whether 8090 kHz was intended as 8060 kHz in interference complaint.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Japanese Foreign Office inquiry whether the complaint on 8090 kHz meant 8060 kHz, as 8090 kHz reportedly involved no interference.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 53 from Joseph C. Grew to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Directs that clarifying telegram to Shanghai and Tokyo be sent by Naval Radio.
subfiles.summary: Treaty Division routing note directing that the telegram concerning 8060 and 8090 kHz frequencies be sent via Naval Radio.
subfiles.title: Treaty Division Routing Slip regarding transmission of telegram

subfiles.about: Clarifies that 8060 kHz is Army frequency and 8090 kHz is Navy frequency, both experiencing interference.
subfiles.summary: Hull clarifies that 8060 kHz is Army and 8090 kHz is Navy, and that Japanese stations interfere with both due to transmitter instability.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 32 from Secretary of State to American Consul General, Shanghai

subfiles.about: Records Navy reports of continuing interference on 8090 kHz and explains distinction between Army and Navy frequencies.
subfiles.summary: Whittington records Navy advice that interference on 8090 kHz from JAQ continues, noting 8060 kHz is an Army frequency under separate protest.
subfiles.title: Treaty Division Memorandum regarding interference on 8090 kHz from station JAQ

subfiles.about: Reports continued serious interference on 8090 kHz from Japanese station JAQ.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of the Navy requests further diplomatic representations after Sixteenth Naval District reports continued serious interference on 8090 kHz from station JAQ.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy to Secretary of State
